biography.plain_text: Philippe de Vilmorin was a French botanist and seed merchant who succeeded his father at Vilmorin-Andrieux in 1899. Trained in natural sciences in Paris, he continued the family’s crop-breeding work and helped organise the International Genetics Conference. He also created the Pézanin arboretum to test trees from around the world.

long_biography.plain_text:
French horticulturist Philippe de Vilmorin recruited young employees for their aptitude and character, then tested them across different jobs. Basic reading, writing and arithmetic were enough to enter his firm. Someone who expected to become a gardener could discover a talent for office work; another might become a travelling representative.

When a promising employee needed specialist knowledge, Vilmorin supported further training through classes, technical school or travel abroad. He believed employers should take an interest in their workers’ futures. Academic qualifications were not his initial selection criterion, but he valued the capacity for further learning that education could develop.
